## Contract review

Head-sha: `59d2196b8cc867339704fd9fa70e79b10770db60`
Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Local-runs: probe — `node scripts/check-adr-symbol-anchors.mjs`, `node scripts/check-adr-links.mjs` and `node scripts/adr-index.mjs --check` on a detached worktree at this head and on a second one at the merge-base 69ce01d7, and `node scripts/pm/check-governed-merges.mjs --pr 28295` from a third worktree at origin/main 53749673, were executed locally, because the two gates this diff can turn red (the anchor count, 2852 at the base to 2930 here; the link count, 944 to 959) are head-versus-base readings no check-run prints as a number, and because every supersede-table quote and every path#symbol anchor had to be seen to resolve against the base and against origin/main; nothing else was built or run, and no test suite was executed.
Scope: docs/adr/0146-studio-designs-setup-administers-one-editor-per-item-paired-customize-package.md (rewritten in place, 303 lines at the base to 628 here; the register's Tier H hit) + the Status line of docs/adr/0005-metadata-customization-overlay.md, docs/adr/0009-metadata-type-contracts.md, docs/adr/0048-package-namespace-and-cross-package-references.md, docs/adr/0126-packaged-metadata-customization-model.md, docs/adr/0131-total-organization-ownership-no-null-organization-id.md and docs/adr/0141-inter-app-dependency-declared-checked-before-install.md (one dated pointer each) + docs/adr/README.md (regenerated index); for the truth of the Context and Decision claims, read at origin/main and not reviewed: packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts (`refusePackagedBaseOverride`, the `allowEnvironmentOverlay` guard), packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-write-package-scope.ts (`resolveWritePackageScope`), packages/metadata-protocol/src/overlay-index.ts, packages/runtime/src/flow-clone.ts (`FLOW_CLONE_STATUS`, the notice), packages/services/service-automation/src/engine.ts (`resolveFlowPrecedence`, `packagedFlowOwner`), packages/services/service-automation/src/resume-target.ts (`resolveResumeTarget`), packages/services/service-automation/src/execution.zod.ts and run-history.ts (`flowVersion` on the run record), packages/objectql/src/registry.ts (`mergeObjectDefinitions`), packages/spec/src/kernel/object-extension.zod.ts (`ObjectExtensionSchema`), packages/spec/src/kernel/namespace-prefix.ts (`deriveNamespaceFromPackageId`), packages/services/service-packages/src/uninstall.ts (`uninstallPackage`, `PackageUninstallExtendedError`), the `sys_metadata_activation` object definition, the fourteen pin-test files the Supersede table and D-items name (existence and the pinned wording, not run); scripts/check-adr-symbol-anchors.mjs, scripts/check-adr-links.mjs and scripts/adr-index.mjs (the gates).

Inputs: card #28237 (body; Wanted 1–6; the seat's claim; no triage comment newer than the dispatch), epic #28236 (body and its comment thread: the eight agreed answers 「等我拍板的 8 个问题，全部同意」, 「四个小问题 同意」, rulings D-1 to D-8, the *Not in this epic* line, the two-minute check), the ruling record 6520616687, sibling cards #28238, #28239, #28240, #28241, #28148, #28149 and the parent #28130; PR #28295 (body: `Fixes #28237`, `Part of #28236`, `Clause-②: no · Metadata-protocol: none`, six 速读 lines, Human Minimum left unchecked for the maintainer; one comment, 6538584753, the seat's claim naming this session and this head, 2026-10-31T03:45Z; no reviews, no hold, no hand-off); PR #28145 (the superseded anchor PR, closed 2026-10-31T02:48Z, its files list); the dispatch order and the dev report at /mnt/project-files/skills-lane-seat2/ (dispatch-28237.md, report-28237.json); .claude/skills/pm-dispatch/references/contract-review.md and review-checklist.md; AGENTS.md Prime Directives #13 and #14 and the *Startup registry reads* section; the full ADR-0146 at this head and at the base; ADR-0005, 0009, 0048, 0126, 0131 and 0141 in full at the base (the text every supersede-table quote is checked against); the code at origin/main for every symbol the Context and Decision sections cite; `git merge-base` of the head and origin/main is 69ce01d7, and origin/main had moved four commits to 53749673 at review time, none of them under docs/adr/ or touching the three ADR scripts; the head's check-runs (three polls, the last at 2026-10-31T03:57Z, all completed); the git log of the branch (one commit over the base, author `Claude`, trailers `Co-Authored-By` and `Claude-Session` present, no model name in the subject).

### ① Derived judgments

1. **Accept set: unchanged — correct.** The diff is ADR prose and the regenerated index only; eight paths, all under docs/adr/; +871 / −225 in the register's count. No schema, export, type or runtime path moves. `Clause-②: no` and `Metadata-protocol: none` hold.
2. **Wanted 1 (the override mechanism) — every point present.** The paired writable package BASE.custom with its dependency declared and its namespace explicit (D3, Q4); the override as a declaration in the item body, `overrides: { package, basedOn }`, whole-document replace, `basedOn` recorded and never judged (D2, Q2, the epic's *Not in this epic* line quoted); undeclared same-name refused at publish (D2, Q1 — but see Must-fix 1 on its scope); the closure rule on `resolveWritePackageScope` (D2); one effective read across the package-less, base-named, layered, list and export reads with the code package always a candidate (D8, the #28238 measurement at d6c0a75f1a cited as Context §5); flows served over the code package's name, rebound in one reload, ledger identity inherited through `sys_metadata_activation (metadata_type, name)`, real version pinning first (D9, Q3); `__c` reserved to BASE.custom and the display-property whitelist (D10, Q7); migration then closure of the package-less write (D11, Q5); the base cannot be uninstalled while the pair exists (D3); the not-done list (D6).
3. **Wanted 2 (what the draft keeps) — kept.** D1 (Studio owns all metadata, Setup administers; the metadata directory moves into Studio at P3), D5 (the app → Studio bridge as a read-only browse entry), D6 (not done, recorded) and D7 (the Setup pages the move owes) are carried from the 2026-10-30 draft with their sentences intact; the toolbar ruling is recorded ahead of the override core where the draft had it. The clone bullet is rewritten to "new similar" only (D4, Q6), which Wanted 1 asked for and #28149's own card text expects.
4. **Wanted 3 (the seven load-bearing symbols) — all anchored, all resolve.** `refusePackagedBaseOverride`, `allowEnvironmentOverlay`, `resolveFlowPrecedence`, `resolveResumeTarget`, `mergeObjectDefinitions`, `ObjectExtensionSchema` and `deriveNamespaceFromPackageId` each carry a path#symbol anchor, and each resolves on origin/main at this head: the probe prints 2930 anchors, 673 symbol (645 declaration, 28 literal), 2210 file-level, exit 0, against 2852 / 148 files at the base — the dev's figures. Three further symbols the prose relies on are written bare and never anchored anywhere in the file: `packagedFlowOwner` (:420), `FLOW_CLONE_STATUS` (:89) and `getMetaItemLayered` (:385). Each exists on origin/main (engine.ts, flow-clone.ts, the metadata read surface), so the prose is true; the gate simply does not hold them (Should-fix 7).
5. **Wanted 4 (the six Status-line pointers) — present, and every recorded sentence survives.** Each of ADR-0005, 0009, 0048, 0126, 0131 and 0141 gains, on its Status line and nowhere else, `· **Superseded in part by [ADR-0146](./0146-….md)** (2026-10-31) — CLAUSE`. A whole-file comparison against the base with the pointer removed: ADR-0005, 0009, 0126 and 0131 are byte-identical; ADR-0048 and ADR-0141 are identical after whitespace folding — their multi-line Status paragraphs (four and five physical lines) were joined to one line so adr-index.mjs, which reads only the physical `**Status**:` line, sees the pointer. ADR-0126's "Original status line follows." sentence is intact and now sits after the pointer. The index regenerates cleanly (`adr-index.mjs --check` exit 0 at the head and the base; Accepted 129 / Proposed 4); the six rows show the pointer in the Supersedes column because the new `**Supersedes in part**:` header matches the index's `/supersedes/i` key, and the "superseded (in part)? … by" reading at adr-index.mjs :244 already accepts the phrase. One cosmetic artefact: ADR-0009's status cell renders "Accepted — · Superseded in part …" because that line's text is "Accepted —" followed by the pointer; the pointer form is the one the card prescribed, so this is noted, not owed.
6. **Wanted 5 (fold the superseded anchor PR) — folded.** PR #28145's three edits (S13 the symbol anchors, S14 the two counted Setup pages, S15 the pointer list) are inside this rewrite: the four symbols it anchored are among the seven of item 4; the two Setup pages are in D7; the pointer list is the Status-line pointers section. #28145 was already closed at 2026-10-31T02:48Z, before the seat claimed this head, so the "close that PR" half of Wanted 5 is done and nothing in the PR body needs to say more.
7. **Wanted 6 (verbatim quotes, anchors on every path) — substantially met, with whitespace defects.** Every maintainer sentence the record marks 「verbatim」 was checked byte for byte against its source (epic #28236 body and comments, the ruling record 6520616687, #28148, #28239, the 2026-10-30 draft). Four carry whitespace the source does not: :15 「…定制都进.custom。」 drops the space the epic has before `.custom`; :359 「…不也是每一个  字段吗」 has a double space where 6520616687 has none; :429 「流程定制只跑新定义、   挂起运行按旧版完成」 has three stray spaces; :442 「扩展字段用  __c 后缀…」 has a double space. The remaining quotes match, or differ only by a line wrap the draft itself introduced and no GitHub source contradicts (Should-fix 6).
8. **Supersede table — every quoted clause is verbatim at the base, and every pin exists on origin/main.** All fifteen quoted clauses across the seven rows (ADR-0005 the five-type tier; ADR-0009 `executionPinned` §2, §2.1 `flow`, §2.4; ADR-0048 §3.3; ADR-0126 D1, D4 wall 1, §7.4, §9 first bullet; ADR-0131 D6; ADR-0141 D3 uninstall item) are substrings of the ADR text at the base after line-join and blockquote-marker normalisation; none is paraphrased inside quotation marks. The fourteen test files named as pins all exist on origin/main, and the sentences the table says they pin are in them. The "two anchors not superseded" paragraph (ADR-0126 D4 walls 2 and 3, ADR-0131 D12) is right: nothing in D2–D11 opens a write onto a managed item outside BASE.custom, and the walled posture is reaffirmed in D3 (403) and D11.
9. **Context §2–§13 — true against origin/main, re-measured here.** §2: `refusePackagedBaseOverride` refuses `NOT_OVERRIDABLE` / `ITEM_LOCKED`, and the only door through it is the `allowEnvironmentOverlay` tier. §3: the overlay index COALESCEs the package-less row over the packaged one. §4: `flow-clone.ts` strips the envelope, `FLOW_CLONE_STATUS` is `draft`, and the notice reads "The copy runs alongside the original…". §5: `packagelessAddress` returns a single candidate, which is the #28238 leak. §6: `resolveFlowPrecedence` warns once and prints the remedy "clone the flow under a new name, or switch the packaged flow off". §7: `resolveResumeTarget` reads `flows.get(run.flowName)` and throws `RUN_NOT_FOUND`; no `getByHash` exists under service-automation/src; the run record already carries `flowVersion` (execution.zod.ts :369, run-history.ts) though resume does not read it, which the record states correctly as "stored and unread". §8: `mergeObjectDefinitions` is additive plus three scalar overrides; `ObjectExtensionSchema` is strict on keys; no `__c` field name exists in packages/ or examples/ today. §9: `deriveNamespaceFromPackageId` takes the last dot segment. §10–§13: `uninstallPackage` throws `PackageUninstallExtendedError` with 409; `sys_metadata_activation` is keyed `(metadata_type, name)`; `packagedFlowOwner` is on the engine; `resolveWritePackageScope` computes the transitive closure. No false claim about current code was found.
10. **Sibling cards — consistent.** #28238 (the undeclared same-name leak) is D8 item 1 plus the unbound-row scope note, verbatim to the card's measurement; #28239 (read-only Studio tools) is D1; #28240 (the closure gate) is D2's closure paragraph — the card names protocol-authoring-gate.ts where the record anchors `resolveWritePackageScope` in protocol-write-package-scope.ts, and the record's anchor is the one that exists on origin/main, so the record is right and the card's file name is stale, not the reverse; #28241 (Setup pages) is D7; #28148 (ledger switch on the item) is D4; #28149 (clone as new similar, copy inactive, Blocked-by N-13) is D4's clone bullet. No sibling contradicts the record.
11. **Internal consistency — one contradiction on the rule N-09 builds (Must-fix 1).** D2 :201–203: "A `.custom` item — or any dependent package's item — that bears a base's item name **without** the declaration is refused when its package publishes". D8 item 2 :387–390: "An item of a dependent package that bears X's name **without** the declaration is not a candidate for X's address at all; it is that package's own item, served under its own address (ADR-0048 §3.3's qualified reference), and refused at publish when it is a `.custom` of X". D9 item 1 :410–412 keeps "shadowing — and warning on — every *undeclared* runtime row of a held name, exactly as today". Three sentences, three answers for the same row: refused at publish for every dependent (D2); served under its own address and refused only for the pair (D8.2); served and warned at runtime (D9.1). The epic's Q1 says only "undeclared same-name refused at publish", and its 为什么改 names the defect as a dependent package's view (not the pair's) silently covering the base's — so D8.2's narrowing to the pair leaves the measured defect outside the refusal, and D2's widening refuses the ADR-0048 §3.3 coexistence the Status pointer says still stands. N-09's card text in the epic ("admit declared, refuse undeclared/out-of-closure/excluded/second declarer") cannot be implemented from this file as it stands.
12. **Citations, numbers and dates.** The quoted rulings are dated 2026-10-30 and 2026-10-31 and precede the Status date; the N-numbers in Rollout match the epic's P0–P3 lists; #28145's closure precedes the claim; every ADR the record cites exists at the base.
13. **PR body declarations.** `Fixes #28237` on its own line; no closing keyword beside any other number. `Clause-②: no`, `Metadata-protocol: none`; the six 速读 lines present. Labels `documentation`, `size/l`, `skip-changeset`; author `objectstack-fleet[bot]`; draft; base `main`.
14. **Register.** `check-governed-merges.mjs --pr 28295` at origin/main: 8 of 8 paths hit docs/adr/**, GOVERNED, Tier H, 871 changed lines under the human-merge threshold.

### ② Semver level

No release. `skip-changeset` is right: the diff publishes nothing from any released package (seven ADR files and the index under docs/adr/, which no package's `files[]` ships); no changeset family is derived for a docs-only diff. On this head `Check Changeset` is success on the labelled run and skipped on its duplicate, the `pr-automation.yml` opt-out. `Clause-②: no` is right; no narrowing is declared or present.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Dev flags: seven items "decided where the rulings were silent", listed in the record's own section and read one by one in ⑤ below; the fleet rule leaves their adjudication to the maintainer, so this record assesses each and rules on none. The dev's report declares no other deviation; the local figures it prints (2930 / 148 against 2852 / 148; 959 against 944; index check OK) are reproduced here exactly.
- Independence: the head was produced on `claude/project-thread-j6cjuw` by the card thread's session; this record is rendered by `session_016WV4d1QkPVVzNz3FJqb2iS`, which did not draft it. Claim 6538584753 names this session and this head; no competing claim, hold or hand-off; no reviews on the PR.
- Author: PR `user.login` is `objectstack-fleet[bot]`; no non-bot login to record.
- Tier: H by the register (docs/adr/**); the maintainer hand-merges. Draft PR; nothing to disarm. The maintainer's 「adr 146 最优先」 and 「28237 现在就插队」 put this card at the front of the queue; a FAIL here is one text fix away from a re-review, and the one must-fix below is a sentence choice, not a redesign.
- CI (46 check-runs on this head, all completed at the last poll, 2026-10-31T03:57Z): 26 success, 20 skipped by path or design, 0 failure, 0 in progress. Success includes both required jobs (`Lint & Repo Gates`, `TypeScript Type Check`) and `Lint · docs & code guards` (runs `check:adr-symbol-anchors`), `Lint · repo & tooling gates` (runs `check:adr-index`), `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `PR-body guards`, `Check Changeset`, `Check Documentation Links`, `Check PR Size`, `Auto Label`. Skipped: the duplicate `Check Changeset`, the UI build, lint, type-check and test shards, Build Docs, Build Core, the opt-in harnesses, the schedule gate, the UI `Live E2E`. The all-green condition for landing is met on this head.
- Merge-base drift: origin/main moved four commits past 69ce01d7 to 53749673 between the branch point and this review; none touches docs/adr/ or the three ADR scripts, so the base readings above are the readings a rebase would give.
- Not re-run here: any test suite (the fourteen pin files were read, not executed); the dev's dispatch-gates families (read from the report; `Lint · PM dispatch-gates` is success on this head).

### ④ Design judgment

Rules face, docs/adr/0146, against its first consumers (the N-08 spec card, the N-09 gate card, the N-10 read card, the N-16 migration card) and against Prime Directive #13:

- **Prime Directive #13 on the six Status edits — hold.** Each edit adds a dated pointer and reverses nothing in place: the recorded sentences of all six Status lines survive (two line-joins and one moved sentence, ①.5), and the clause each pointer names is quoted verbatim in the Supersede table. This is the amended-status-line route #13 prescribes. "Superseded in part by" has no prior use in docs/adr/ — the corpus writes "Superseded by" and "Amended by" — but the index reader already accepts the phrase, the card prescribed it, and it names precisely what the table does. One wording wobble: ADR-0009's pointer says "Superseded in part" while the record's own table row says "Nothing in ADR-0009 is reversed" — the resume reading is narrowed, the contract is not; "Amended by" is the corpus's word for that (Should-fix 4).
- **Prime Directive #13 on the in-place rewrite — hold, with one locator owed.** The 2026-10-30 draft was Proposed, never Accepted, so #13 does not bind its sentences; the record keeps the draft's D1, D5, D6, D7 and the two-editors finding intact and names what it replaced ("rewritten in place from the Proposed draft of 2026-10-30", D2/D3/D4 renamed). The corpus's precedents for a rewrite (ADR-0048 "Revised", ADR-0126's "Original status line follows", ADR-0131's recorded rejected drafts) each say where the earlier text can be read; this record names the draft's date but not its commit or PR (#28045), so a reader who wants the Proposed D2–D4 has nothing to follow (Should-fix 5). ADR-0141 is the precedent for the "decided where the rulings were silent … merging accepts them; an objection names the number" section, and the form here matches it.
- **First consumer — the rule is one document except where ①.11 says.** A spec author (N-08) reads one declaration shape, one namespace rule, one `__c` rule and one whitelist criterion; a read author (N-10) reads five read kinds and one selection rule; a migration author (N-16) reads an idempotent per-base ceremony with a stated predicate. The gate author (N-09) reads three rules for the undeclared same-name row and must choose; that is the must-fix.
- **Execution plan — complete and ordered.** Rollout P0–P3 names every card by N-number and the epic's issue where one exists, orders the override core after this record and N-05, Studio customization after P1, and the Setup retirements at P3 after the landing counts; the not-done list (D6) closes the doors the maintainer closed (action ledger switch, upgrade diff, Studio write on read-only packages).
- **Where the record's reasoning leans on a rule it misreads (Should-fix 1, 2).** D3 "Dependency range" and merge item 1 argue from ADR-0141 D2 as if it gated a base upgrade: "a base upgrade within its major keeps the pair valid at ADR-0141 D2's gate" and "`*` would let a major upgrade of the base pass ADR-0141 D2's gate". ADR-0141 D2's pre-install check runs at install acts of the dependent and never on a base upgrade; interception of an upgrade is what D3 defers. The decision (`^major`) may still be the right one, but its stated reason is not a reason, and the maintainer reads the reason to accept the item. D10 and merge item 7 say a vendor's next version "can never take that name" because `__c` is refused "at publish and at `os validate`"; a vendor artifact enters an environment through `installPackage` and the marketplace's install-local door, neither of which runs publish or `os validate`, so "never" is not enforced as written unless the install door is named too.
- **One clause the table should carry (Should-fix 3).** ADR-0126 §7.1's "⛔ No same-name clone in a second package" is a recorded prohibition on exactly the shape D2 now permits when declared (a same-name item in BASE.custom). The table lifts §7.4 and §9's first bullet but leaves §7.1 standing, so ADR-0126 still forbids what ADR-0146 D2 allows.
- **D2's type list (observation; see ⑤).** The list names `action` among the overridable types with no condition, while ADR-0126 §3 puts `action` in Regime C (behavioural) and D4 of this record keeps the action ledger switch out of the epic. `flow`, the other behavioural type, gets D9's four conditions; `action` gets none. Not a contradiction with a ruling, but an open edge the maintainer should see.
- **Not touched by this review**: the rendering of the regenerated README beyond the one artefact in ①.5; the dev's choice of N-number ordering inside P1.

### ⑤ The seven items the record decides where it says the rulings were silent

Listed for the maintainer with the ADR text, the dev's choice, the alternatives a reader would weigh, and whether the item is in fact silent in the rulings. Nothing here is a ruling.

1. **The pair's dependency range** (D3 :260–262; merge item 1). Dev's choice: `^major` of the base's `manifest.version` at creation. Alternatives: `*` (what #28238's measurement used for the dependent package), an exact pin (refuses every patch upgrade of the base, as the record says), a floor at the installed version with no ceiling. Silent: yes — epic ruling D-3 says "dependency on the base declared" and no comment names a range. Assessment: the choice is defensible as a reversible middle, but the stated rationale rests on ADR-0141 D2 gating base upgrades, which it does not (④); the item should be re-argued from what the range actually does today (it is read at install of the pair and at `os validate`, and it is what a future upgrade interception would read).
2. **`basedOn` recorded, never judged** (D2 :194–197; merge item 2). Dev's choice: no door compares it, nothing is refused on it. Alternatives: none the rulings leave open. Silent: no — the epic's *Not in this epic* line says "upgrade diff / basedOn checking (recorded only)", and the record quotes it. Assessment: already decided; it belongs in the record as a carried ruling, not as a merge question.
3. **The uninstall refusal's shape** (D3; merge item 3). Dev's choice: 409 from `uninstallPackage`'s existing `PackageUninstallExtendedError` family, one envelope, two causes. Alternatives: a new error code in the same family; 422 as a validation refusal. Silent: yes on the shape; the ADR-0141 merge-question-5 reasoning for the extender case chose 409 for "another package still stands on this one", and the record extends that reasoning to the pair. Assessment: consistent with the precedent; the least-surprising answer.
4. **The display-property class by criterion, not list** (D10 :447–; merge item 4). Dev's choice: a property is admitted when changing it changes no DDL, no stored value, no validation verdict and no permission; the N-08 spec card enumerates the members against `FieldSchema`. Alternatives: enumerate the list in the ADR now; or leave both the criterion and the list to the card. Silent: Q7 says "limited to a display-property whitelist" and names no members; the criterion is the record's. Assessment: the criterion is the right thing for an ADR to fix and the list the right thing for the spec card; the maintainer should know that "whitelist" in Q7 is being read as "a class with a membership test" rather than "an enumerated list in this record".
5. **One address for the override, base reachable as the layered `code` layer** (D8 item 2; merge item 5). Dev's choice: all five read kinds serve the declared override within the base's address; the base document stays reachable only as the layered read's `code` layer. Alternatives: a second address for the override; a dedicated "original" read. Silent: largely not — card #28237 Wanted 1 asks for "one effective read" across the five kinds, and the epic's two-minute check says 「三处读取同一列集、导出带声明…」. Assessment: decided by the card and the epic; the record restates it as a merge item, which is harmless but overstates the silence.
6. **Migration as an idempotent per-base CLI ceremony, not a boot step** (D11; merge item 6). Dev's choice: ADR-0131 D10's shape, invoked by an administrator, reports per base. Alternatives: a Setup or Studio admin action (ADR-0070 D5 said "A small migration (or admin action)"); a boot step (rejected by AGENTS.md *Startup registry reads*, as the record says). Silent: Q5 says only "closed after the migration"; the vehicle is the record's. Assessment: the CLI shape is the corpus's precedent and the boot shape is barred; the one open question is whether the console also needs a button for a customer without CLI access, which N-16 can answer.
7. **`__c` refused outside BASE.custom at publish and at `os validate`** (D10 :440–443; merge item 7). Dev's choice: two enforcement points. Alternatives: add the install door (`installPackage` and marketplace install-local) so a vendor artifact is refused on entry; add a Studio-side courtesy refusal for a non-pair package. Silent: who may use the suffix is ruled (「扩展字段用 __c 后缀，只有 .custom 包能用。」); where it is enforced is the record's. Assessment: as written, the "never" claim is not met for a vendor artifact (④); the maintainer should either accept the two points and soften "never", or ask for the install door.

Two edges the record decides without flagging: D2's type list (`action`, `app`, `page` among the overridable types, with conditions only on `flow`), and the scope of Q1's refusal (every dependent package versus the pair only — the must-fix).

Implemented-by: `claude/project-thread-j6cjuw`
Reviewed-by: `session_016WV4d1QkPVVzNz3FJqb2iS`

**VERDICT: FAIL**

Must-fix:
1. Make D2 (:201–203), D8 item 2 (:387–390) and D9 item 1 (:410–412) say one rule for an undeclared same-name item of a dependent package that is not the pair: either it is refused at publish like the pair's (then D8.2's "served under its own address" clause and D9.1's "keeps shadowing — and warning on" go, and the ADR-0048 §3.3 pointer says so), or it is served under its own address and only the pair's is refused (then D2's "— or any dependent package's item —" goes, and the record says how the #28238 defect, which is a non-pair dependent's view, is closed — D8 item 1 alone, or not in this epic).
